properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — 2026-08-11, from Anthony bringing the Defense Acquisition University criteria for a good requirement into the discussion. Nothing here is intent.

THE CRITERIA HE CITED, in his framing. Individual requirement: NECESSARY (addresses a true operational gap), UNAMBIGUOUS (everyone reads it the same way), VERIFIABLE/TESTABLE (has criteria that can be practically proven), FEASIBLE (achievable within technology and budget), IMPLEMENTATION-FREE (what the system must deliver, not how to build it), MEASURABLE (quantifiable data, not vague adjectives). Full set: COMPLETE, CONSISTENT, TRACEABLE.

WHAT REFLOW2 ACTUALLY CHECKS, sorted against that list:
  SET-LEVEL — partially covered, structurally
    Traceable   forward only, via the golden thread. Backward is unchecked — see
                dec:idea-should-a-requirement-trace-back-to-its-demand-signal
    Consistent  partially, via CONTRADICTS and dimension drift
    Complete    approximated by the gap detectors, never claimed
  INDIVIDUAL — ZERO OF SIX. Necessary, Unambiguous, Verifiable, Feasible, Implementation-Free and
    Measurable are all properties of the TEXT, and no reflow2 computation reads requirement text
    for quality at all. `unverified_capability` is the nearest thing and it asks whether a check
    EXISTS, never whether the requirement is phrased so that a check is POSSIBLE — a different
    question with the same words in it.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Nothing changes; state the boundary explicitly somewhere a user will read it, so "reflow2 does
    not grade your prose" is a known limit rather than a surprise.
(b) A three-party check: the LLM judges the six against the text, the graph records the judgement
    and who made it, the human decides. Fits dec:three-party-checks exactly and needs no new
    detector.
(c) A deterministic subset only — e.g. MEASURABLE is partly mechanical (does the statement contain
    a number and a unit?), and IMPLEMENTATION-FREE has weak mechanical tells. Cheap, and cheap in
    the bad way: a keyword heuristic that grades prose will be wrong confidently.

⭐ THE ARGUMENT FOR (a)/(b) OVER ANY DETECTOR: `req:deterministic-core` is accepted — the core is
deterministic and LLM-free. Judging "is this unambiguous" is irreducibly a language judgement. So
the six do not belong in detect.rs at all; if they belong anywhere it is the skill layer, where an
LLM already reads and the human already decides.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-EXAMPLE, recorded because it cuts against the whole frame. Of the storyflow
feedback's three ranked asks, #1 was NOT implementation-free — it named the mechanism outright
("model VERIFIES onto DesignRule") — and it is the one that got built. #2 and #3 were stated as
node-type wishes and did not. So on this evidence MEASURABLE and VERIFIABLE predicted delivery and
IMPLEMENTATION-FREE anti-predicted it. When the system under design IS the modelling vocabulary,
"what not how" gets genuinely slippery, and applying DAU to reflow2's own requirements needs that
caveat or it will reject the requirements that work.
properties.name: OPEN — does reflow2 have any opinion on whether a Requirement is WELL WRITTEN, and if so whose job is it?
properties.rationale: Anthony brought a mature external standard to bear and it partitions cleanly: reflow2 covers the set-level characteristics structurally and none of the six individual ones, because those are text judgements and the core is deliberately LLM-free. Whether that boundary is a deliberate design position or an unnoticed hole has never been stated either way.
